The Criminal Application is heard finally with the consent of the learned counsel appearing for the parties.

3. This is an application seeking to quash and set aside the Charge-sheet No.55 of 2023 dated 13th of March,2023 arising out of First Information Report vide Crime 1157 of 2022 registered with the Police Station Awadhutwadi, District Yavatmal for the offence punishable under Sections 325,323,
498-A, 504 and 506 r/w 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
4. The applicants are in laws and relatives of the husband of the non-applicant No.2-informant lady.

The applicant Nos.1 and 2 are Kavita apl(2)-386-23.odt parents-in-law, applicant No.3 is brother-in-law, applicant No.4 is the wife of applicant No.3, applicant No.5 is sister-in-law and applicant No.6 is the brother of the applicant No.2 i.e. maternal uncle of the husband of the non-applicant No.2.
The allegations are about mental and physical harassment by all applicants along with her husband, who is not before this Court.

5. Brief facts of the case are as under:-
The marriage of non-applicant No.2 was performed with accused No.1 i.e. Shrikant Prakash Deshmukh on 11.02.2019.
Initially, informant stayed for 15 days in the joint family at Akola with the husband and applicant Nos.2 and 3.
Thereafter, the couple stayed at Aurangabad as the husband was employed at Aurangabad.
Informant alleges that her husband used to quarrel and beat her for the reason that her father has not offered valuables in the marriage.
He used to abuse her parents in filthy language.
Her husband did not allow her to talk with the neighbours and used to beat Prakashrao S/O Daulatrao Deshmukh And 5 ... vs State Of Mah. Thr. Pso Awadhutwadi ...

It is alleged that husband used to throw cooked food and plate on her person.
Once, he beat her in presence of applicant Nos.1 and 2 but they remained to be silent spectator.
It is alleged that her husband became more aggressive and was insisting for divorce.
On refusal, he slapped at her ear followed by Kavita apl(2)-386-23.odt internal injury.
Thereafter, all applicants also insisted her for divorce and instigate her husband to harass and therefore, she has lodged the report against all applicants on which the crime has been registered.
6. The learned counsel appearing for the applicants would submit that merely omnibus allegations have been levelled against all the applicants.
No specific allegation is made against either of the applicant.
Informant never stated specific role of the applicant Nos.1 to 7, who are relatives of the husband.

The allegations against applicant No.7, who is maternal uncle of the husband are that he asked informant to give divorce as her father did not give the valuables by saying that the husband of applicant No.4 has received many articles from her maternal house.
These are the only allegations against the applicant No.7.
Only because the names are stated and general allegations are made about instigation.
7. The learned APP has opposed the application stating that there are specific allegations against all the applicants.
Though they were present when her husband beat her, they did not restrain him but instigated to beat.
The allegation about demand is also made.
It is for trial to decide the worth of allegations.
Hence prayed to reject the application.
Kavita apl(2)-386-23.odt 8.

The counsel for non-applicant No.2 has also opposed the application stating that the husband of the non-applicant No.2 has treated her with cruelty and all these applicants instigated him and asked to take divorce.
The applicant Nos. 7 and non-applicant No.2 asked her to give divorce as she has not brought anything from her parental house.
The specific allegations are there they have to defend it during the period of trial and prove their innocence.
Therefore, this is not a case to quash and set aside the Charge-sheet.
Hence, prayed to reject the application.

9. Heard the learned counsel appearing for applicant and non- applicant No.2 as well as the learned APP for the State.
10.
The offence under Section 498-A of the Indian penal Code is registered by making allegation against these applicants that they instigated her husband for treating her with cruelty.
No doubt, the incidents are mentioned by the non applicant No.2 about beating and throwing the hot vegetable on her person amounting to cruelty.
All these allegations are against the husband.
The husband is not before us.

11. Before we delve into detail on the nature and contents of allegations made against these applicants, it becomes pertinent to mention that incorporation of Section 498-A of IPC was aimed at Kavita apl(2)-386-23.odt preventing cruelty committed upon a woman by her husband and her in-laws, by facilitating rapid state intervention.

sentences.text: significantly and there is a greater disaffection and friction surrounding the institution of marriage.
This has resulted in an increased tendency to employ provisions of Section such as 498-A IPC as instruments to settle personal scores against the husband and his relatives.

Section 498-A provides that:-
498-A.:- Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty- Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine.

Explanation:- for the purpose of this Section, cruelty means - (a) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or (b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand."
12. As per the allegations made against these applicants, whether it amounts to cruelty defined under Section 498-A of the Indian Penal Code is required to be considered.
No specific allegations are made Kavita apl(2)-386-23.odt against any of the applicants.
13. The allegations are made by the non-applicant No.2 that her husband used to say that if she delivers the baby, it would be given to applicant No.3 i.e. the brother of the husband.
It is not the case of the non-applicant No.2 that the applicant Nos.3 and 4 forced her to give her baby.

Mere statement of her husband that he wanted to hand over the baby to the applicant Nos. 3 and 4 is not sufficient to establish the cruelty against respondent Nos.3 and 4 as they have not stated anything about it.
The presence of applicant Nos.1 and 2 at the time when her husband beat her cannot be said to be cruelty at the hands of applicant Nos.1 and 2.
Nothing is there in the FIR against all these applicants.

14. The learned counsel appearing for the applicants has relied on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam and ors. Vs.State of Bihar and ors. 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 141 in which it is observed that :-

sentences.text: "The above-mentioned decisions clearly demonstrate that this court has at numerous instances expressed concern over the misuse of section 498A IPC and the increased tendency of implicating relatives of the husband in matrimonial disputes, without analysing the long term ramifications of a trial on the complainant as well as the accused.

It is further manifest from the said judgments that false implication by way of general omnibus allegations made in the course of matrimonial Kavita Prakashrao S/O Daulatrao Deshmukh And 5 ... vs State Of Mah. sentences.text: Therefore, this court by way of its judgments has warned the courts from proceeding against the relatives and in-laws of the husband when no prima facie case is made out against them".
15. On perusal of the facts of the case in hand, and the contents in the First Information Report, it reveals that the general allegations are levelled against the applicants.
The first informant alleged that all the accused harassed her mentally and physically.
No specific and distinct allegations have been made against either of the applicants to constitute the offence under Section 498-A of the Indian Penal Code.
This simply leads to a situation, wherein one fails to ascertain the role played by each accused in furtherance of the offence.
The allegations are therefore general and omnibus and can at best be said to have been made out on account of small skirmishes.
Insofar as husband is concerned, since he is not before us, we have not examined the veracity of allegations made against him.
However, as far as the applicants are concerned, the allegations made against them being general and omnibus, do not warrant prosecution.

Therefore, upon consideration of the relevant circumstances and in the absence of specific role attributed to the applicants, it would be unjust if the applicants are forced to go through the tribulations of a trial, i.e., general and omnibus allegations cannot manifest in a situation where the relatives of the husband of first Kavita apl(2)-386-23.odt informant are forced to undergo trial.
It has been highlighted by this Court, that a criminal trial leading to an eventual acquittal also inflicts severe scars upon the accused, and such an exercise must therefore be discouraged.
16. In view of the above facts and discussion, the Criminal Application is allowed.
17. Charge-sheet No.55 of 2023 dated 13 th of March,2023

arising out of First Information Report vide Crime 1157 of 2022 registered with the Police Station Awadhutwadi, District Yavatmal for the offence punishable under Sections 325,323, 498-A, 504 and 506 r/w 34 of the Indian Penal Code against the present applicants is hereby quashed and set aside.
18. Criminal Application stands disposed of.
